name: HAL+ (CCSD)
description: An integrated infrastructure for the dissemination and long-term preservation of research results, spanning HAL, Sciencesconf, and Episciences, operated by CCSD (Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe).

coverage.notes: HAL+ is multi-disciplinary and is aimed at all those involved in the research process, whether they are researchers, institutions, funding bodies, publishers or infrastructures.

stakeholder-governed.notes: Inclusive and shared, the governance is open to all HAL+ stakeholders and international in scope.

non-discriminatory.notes: Governance includes the Ministry of Higher Education and Research, the three supervisory bodies (CNRS, Inria, INRAE), and each institution that contributes financially appoints its representative to the Assembly of Partners.

transparent-governance.notes: The names and functions of the members of the committees that make up the governance are posted on the CCSD website and on the Episciences website.

cannot-lobby.notes: No lobbying activities are undertaken by HAL+ and the CCSD.

living-will.notes: The CNRS archiving plan foresees the transfer of all data to the national archives in case the CCSD and HAL are closed, but a study is still underway on long-term preservation for Episciences, whose articles are hosted in archives that do not yet guarantee longevity.

regular-review.notes: Not addressed as a distinct item in HAL+'s published self-assessment (assessed against POSI v1.1, which did not include this as a separate governance principle).

transparent-operations.notes: Not addressed as a distinct item in HAL+'s published self-assessment.

time-limited-funds.notes: Recurrent support from the Ministry is complemented by project-based funding, such as HALiance, a five-year project funded by the French National Research Agency.

generate-surplus.notes: Explicitly not applicable: as a service financed by public bodies, HAL+ is not intended to generate surplus funds.

financial-reserves.notes: Marked not applicable in HAL+'s self-assessment.

mission-consistent-revenue.notes: The management and development of HAL+ are part of the CCSD's mission.

revenue-not-data.notes: Data may be used without financial compensation. The contribution of institutions that have a HAL portal is indexed to the number of researchers, not to data access.

volunteer-labour.notes: Not addressed in HAL+'s published self-assessment.

transition-planning.notes: Not addressed as a distinct item; the closest related content is the Living Will's CNRS archiving plan.

open-source.notes: HAL+ uses many free, open tools (Linux Debian, Proxmox, MySQL, Solr, Apache, Nginx); Episciences' own code is GPL v3.0, while HAL's own codebase is currently being migrated to the open-source Symfony framework as part of the HALiance project.

open-secure-data.notes: Metadata is available under a CC0 licence. Licences are associated with submitted files in accordance with authors' rights.

available-preserved.notes: HAL data can be harvested via the OAI-PMH server, accessible via open APIs.

patent-non-assertion.notes: HAL+ does not hold any patent. If it were to apply for one, the CCSD is prepared to give a non-assertion undertaking.

interoperability-standards.notes: Not addressed as a distinct item in HAL+'s published self-assessment (assessed against POSI v1.1, which did not include this as a separate principle).
